title: Design a ride-hailing app like Uber
question: How would you design a ride hailing app like Uber?

problem.statement: Design a ride-hailing service like Uber: a rider asks for a ride, the system finds a nearby driver, and both follow each other on a live map until the trip ends.
example: A rider requests a ride from a pickup point
Both see live locations and an arrival time
constraints: 5 million active drivers, each sending a location every 4 seconds
A driver must never get two rides at once
problem.followUp: How do you find the drivers within 2 km of a rider in milliseconds?

steps.caption: What the interviewer is really asking.

plain.asking: Know where every driver is *right now*, find the closest free ones to a rider quickly, and make sure each driver gets only one ride at a time.
points: *Must be fast:* matching, while soaking up a flood of location updates.
*Out of scope:* payments, surge pricing, driver sign-up.

check.question: The rider is right at the edge of their cell. Why search the neighbouring cells too?
options: The closest driver may sit just across the edge
Neighbouring cells are cheaper to read
check.explain: Cells are just a filing system. A driver 50 m away *across the border* lives in the next cell, so always check the ring around the rider.

check.question: Two matchers pick the same driver at the same moment. What makes sure only one gets them?
options: An atomic reserve-if-free with a timeout
check.explain: Checking and claiming happen as *one step*, so the second matcher sees “reserved” and moves on to the next driver.
